claim: The shared WebSocket sender pool of at most 16 threads, each blocked up to TinyHttpd's 30 s write timeout on a stalled session, means 16 non-reading clients (one per sender thread) block outbound messages to every other session for up to 30 s. That breaks D-320 ('a slow client SHALL not block sends to other sessions') and is easy to trigger on purpose.

D-419 requires a configurable WebSocket pong timeout and D-416 budgets a NaruServe scheduler for WebSocket pings, but TinyHttpd's read loop sends its own ping when a read times out after pingInterval and closes with 1001 after a second timeout. Any frame clears awaitingPong, and WebSocketListener has no pong callback. NaruServe cannot see Pong frames, so it cannot enforce a pong timeout separate from the ping interval. Also, a connection that answers pings never idles out inside TinyHttpd.

TinyHttpd returns 501 only for CONNECT whose target is not origin-form. 'CONNECT /path HTTP/1.1' passes the parser and reaches the NaruServe handler, so 'CONNECT is always answered 501 by TinyHttpd's parser' is false, and an enable policy would route origin-form CONNECT on TinyHttpd.

The 339-thread budget says the acceptor and watchdog threads each request a 256 KiB stack. TinyHttpd creates both with the platform default stack. Only pool workers use workerStackBytes. The memory figure recorded in defaults.md for API 21 would be wrong.

shutdown() is defined for RUNNING (D-161) and NEW (D-164), but not for an app that is STARTING (a listen() in progress on another thread, for example Android onDestroy during startup) or FAILED. The concurrency tests for D-153/T46 hit this case.
evidence: object.md:11.3 state diagram (no STARTING->shutdown edge); docs/api/lifecycle.md:136-141

claim: object.md §9.4 says the default cache policy can be set as a server-wide security policy, next to the example defaults for authenticated REST (no-store). D-410 limits the configurable default to static responses, so a REST no-store default has no item.

claim: object.md §9.3 makes a combined Range + cache test mandatory, for example Range with If-None-Match or If-Range, or cache headers on 206. The Range items and cache items are tested separately, and no item requires the combination.
D-238 requires a bounded urlencoded body limit, but no item gives its default, configuration API or the wave that decides it. I-011 and I-012 need a concrete default recorded in defaults.md.

object.md §14.3 asks for a per-adapter TLS/WSS review and separate Android 5 TLS testing. TinyHttpd supports TLS (TlsConfig, Builder.tls), but no item decides whether v1 exposes TLS or records it as post-v1, and req.isSecure() can only ever be false on the embedded adapter.
